transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, I came in because I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. It's getting really bad. My kitchen table is completely covered with things... my husband's appointment papers, flyers from church, notes from the senior center, and these half-finished lists I make. I just sit there looking at it all, not knowing which thing to do first, and before I know it, the whole day is just gone.
Do you find it hard to stay organized or focused on tasks in other parts of your life, like work or personal responsibilities, or does this mainly happen with paperwork and lists at home?

It's everywhere, really, not just the paperwork on the kitchen table. It's gotten to the point where... well, I actually had to step down and give up leading a big event at the senior center because I just couldn't manage it all. And as for my personal responsibilities, my daughter has started double-checking my bills and our appointments. She just doesn't trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore. So, yes, it's definitely affecting other parts of my life.
Looking back, would you say that problems with staying focused or being overly active have been with you since childhood, or do you think this is something that started more recently in your life?

Well, I think it's always been there, honestly. Even as a little girl, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always forgetting my books or my homework. They constantly had to remind me to just finish my seatwork so I could go outside for recess. So, yes, it's not really a new thing, it's just... harder to manage now, I suppose.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be doing something all the time, or find it hard to sit still for long periods?

Yes, I do. It's... well, it's hard for me to just sit quietly. Even when I’m really trying to sit politely in a meeting, I'll catch myself rubbing my hands together, or tapping my foot. I might be clicking my pen or just shifting around in my chair so much that people actually look over at me. I don't always realize I'm doing it right away, but I just can't seem to stay completely still.
Can you think of other situations, like at church or in social gatherings, where your restlessness or trouble staying focused has been noticeable or caused problems?

Well, yes, it definitely happens in other situations. During volunteer meetings, or even just sitting at the table for supper, I have a really hard time just staying in my chair. I keep getting up to check the calendar on the wall, or to look for a specific piece of paper, or to refill my water glass... or really just to move around. I do it even when I know I’m supposed to just stay seated and listen to whoever is talking. I just can't seem to stay put.
Do you find it difficult to stay focused when you're doing something that requires your full attention for a longer period, like reading a book, watching a movie, or having a conversation?

You know, I haven't really noticed a problem with that. If I sit down to read a book or watch a movie, I can usually follow along just fine. And with conversations... well, I don't think I have a hard time paying attention when I'm talking to someone. So, no, I wouldn't say that's really an issue for me.
